spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Fort.Yukon: Fort Yukon Magnetometer is a ground geomagnetic observatory at Fort Yukon, Alaska (IAGA code FYU), operating at least from the 1970s into the late 1980s, measuring vector geomagnetic field variations for ionospheric, auroral, and magnetospheric studies in the high-latitude Alaska sector; it is part of IAGA/CDAWeb ground magnetometer holdings.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Rankin.Inl: Rankin Inlet (IAGA code RIT) is a ground geomagnetic observatory at Rankin Inlet, Nunavut, Canada, with CDAWeb/INTERMAGNET records from at least the 2010s to present. It measures local vector geomagnetic-field variations for ionospheric current, auroral, and magnetospheric disturbance studies; it has no orbital phases.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/St.Johns: St. John’s (STJ) is an IAGA/INTERMAGNET ground magnetometer observatory at St. John’s, Newfoundland, Canada, operational by 1968 and still active. It has no orbit; from its fixed North Atlantic site it records geomagnetic field components and variations used for ionospheric, magnetospheric, auroral, and space-weather studies.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Barrow: The Barrow (BRW) geomagnetic observatory, operational since about 1949 at Barrow/Utqiaġvik, Alaska, is a ground-based high-latitude magnetometer station. It records local vector geomagnetic field variations for studies of auroral-zone ionospheric currents, magnetospheric disturbances, substorms, and space-weather activity, as part of the IAGA/INTERMAGNET-style observatory network.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Dombas: Dombås (DOB) is a ground geomagnetic observatory at Dombås, Norway, operational since at least the 1980s with CDAWeb/IMAGE digital coverage mainly from the 1990s onward. It measures local three-component magnetic field variations for studies of ionospheric currents, auroral electrojets, geomagnetic storms, and high-latitude magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/College: The College (CMO) geomagnetic observatory, operating since 1948 at the University of Alaska Fairbanks/College site near Fairbanks, Alaska, is a fixed ground station in the auroral zone. It measures continuous vector and scalar geomagnetic field variations for ionospheric, magnetospheric, auroral, and space-weather studies and contributes data to IAGA/INTERMAGNET.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Iqaluit: Iqaluit (IQA) is a fixed ground-based IAGA/INTERMAGNET geomagnetic observatory at Iqaluit, Nunavut, Canada, with digital data available from 1992 and continuing. It measures local vector geomagnetic-field variations for auroral-zone ionospheric current, geomagnetic-storm, and magnetospheric studies; its observing location has not changed.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Lovozero: The Lovozero (LOV) magnetometer is a ground-based geomagnetic station at Lovozero on Russia’s Kola Peninsula (~68.0°N, 35.0°E), operating by the early 1990s and contributing to the IMAGE/IAGA network. It measures ground magnetic-field variations for auroral, ionospheric-current, substorm, and magnetosphere–ionosphere coupling studies; it has no orbital phases.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Ivalo: The Ivalo magnetometer (IVA), operational in IMAGE/CDAWeb records from at least 1994, is a fixed ground station near Ivalo, northern Finland, measuring geomagnetic field variations for auroral, ionospheric, and magnetospheric studies. It is part of the IMAGE high-latitude magnetometer network and contributes IAGA-style ground magnetic data.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Fredericks: Fredericksburg (FRD) is a USGS/IAGA ground geomagnetic observatory near Fredericksburg/Corbin, Virginia, USA, operating since 1956. It continuously records local vector magnetic-field variations and absolute geomagnetic measurements for geomagnetic storms, quiet-time variations, and space-weather studies; as a fixed ground station, it has no orbital phases.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Meanook: The Meanook Magnetometer (IAGA code MEA) is a ground geomagnetic observatory near Meanook/Athabasca, Alberta, Canada, operating since 1916. It has no orbit; fixed magnetometers measure the local vector magnetic field and its variations for studies of geomagnetic storms, magnetospheric/ionospheric currents, pulsations, and space weather.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Anchorage: Anchorage is an IAGA ground geomagnetic observatory in Anchorage, Alaska, operational from at least the IGY era in 1957, measuring local magnetic-field variations for ionospheric, magnetospheric, and space-weather studies; it has no orbit or changing vantage point.
spase://SMWG/Observatory/IAGA/Shumagin: Shumagin (SHU) is a USGS/IAGA ground geomagnetic observatory in the Shumagin Islands near Sand Point, Alaska, operational since about 2003. It has no orbit; it records local vector geomagnetic field variations for magnetospheric, ionospheric, auroral, and space-weather studies.
